title: Treatment of children with the Sentio bone conduction implant – surgical feasibility and audiological results
summary:
Hearing loss can have numerous causes, and in many instances, it can be effectively managed with conventional hearing aids. However, there are some less common types of hearing loss—such as severe hearing loss or damage to the ear's anatomy—where conventional hearing aids may not provide any benefit. In these cases, bone conduction implants are used, which transmit sound through the bones instead of the ear. 
Early restoration of hearing is crucial, particularly in children, as it supports normal speech development and social engagement. Unfortunately, the use of bone conduction implants is largely dependent on individual anatomy, and only a limited number of implants are approved for children, especially those under the age of 12. This study aims to evaluate the usability of a bone conduction implant that is already approved for children older than 12 years. 
To achieve this, we will assess both the feasibility of the surgical procedure and the patients' hearing abilities. The feasibility will be evaluated based on the duration of the operation, any deviations from standard procedures, and complications that may arise. Additionally, preoperative and postoperative tone and speech audiograms will be used to measure hearing ability. All of this data will be collected as part of the routine clinical treatment for the condition.
conditions: Patients under 12 years of age and patients between 12 and 16 years of age who receive a Sentio implant as part of standard care

interventions.name: Arm 1: For patients <12, the implantation (duration of surgery, deviations from standard, complications) of a Sentio implant system from Oticon and the improvement in hearing (pre- and post-operative tone and speech audiograms) will be evaluated.

Arm 2: For patients between 12 and 16 years of age, the implantation (duration of surgery, deviations from the standard, complications) of a Sentio implant system from Oticon and the improvement in hearing (pre- and post-operative tone and speech audiograms) will be evaluated.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Receive Sentio implants as standard care
Exclusion criteria:
All patients without a Sentio implant in standard care and patients generally under 2 and over 16 years of age.
